items.title: Bangladesh holds first election since 2024 uprising ousted Hasina

featured_image.name: Is BNP’s Tarique Rahman the change post-Hasina Bangladesh is looking for?

items.description:
Bangladesh heads to the polls on Thursday in its first national election since a student-led uprising toppled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August 2024. More than 127 million voters will cast ballots in 299 constituencies, choosing between the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and an alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, while Hasina's Awami League remains barred from participating.

The election will also feature a simultaneous referendum on the July Charter, a document proposing constitutional reforms including a 10-year lifetime cap for prime ministers and expanded presidential powers. Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus, the Nobel Peace Prize laureate who has led the interim government since Hasina's ouster, urged voters on Monday to support the charter, saying a "yes" vote would build Bangladesh's future "in a more positive way."[1]

items.title: Russia launches 'massive' missile attack on Kyiv, killing one

featured_image.name: Kyiv hit by 'massive' Russian missile, drone attack ...

items.description:
The Ukrainian capital Kyiv came under a "massive" Russian missile attack early Thursday morning, with Mayor Vitali Klitschko reporting that residential and non-residential buildings on both sides of the Dnipro River were hit as explosions echoed throughout the city.

"A mass attack on the capital is still underway," Klitschko said on Telegram, announcing that emergency medical teams had been dispatched to respond to the assault. The attack killed one person and injured four others, including a 9-year-old child, in the Obolonskyi district, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Cisco raises revenue forecast, launches AI networking chip
items.description:
Cisco lifted its annual revenue forecast and unveiled a powerful new networking chip on Wednesday, underscoring how surging demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure is driving growth across its business.

The company now expects fiscal 2026 revenue between $61.2 billion and $61.7 billion, up from prior guidance of $60.2 billion to $61 billion. The raised outlook follows a second quarter in which the networking giant reported record revenue of $15.3 billion, a 10 percent increase compared with the same period last year.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: NASA detects water and organic molecules on interstellar comet

featured_image.name: Comet 3I/ATLAS from beyond solar system carries key molecule ...

items.description:
A cosmic wanderer from beyond our solar system is offering scientists an unprecedented window into how planets form around distant stars. Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, only the third confirmed interstellar object ever observed, has yielded a bounty of discoveries including the first detection of water activity from such an object, along with organic molecules and a distinctive carbon-rich composition that is reshaping our understanding of planetary building blocks across the galaxy.

The findings, announced in studies published this week, suggest that the chemical ingredients for life may be common throughout the cosmos. "When we detect water — or even its faint ultraviolet echo, OH — from an interstellar comet, we're reading a note from another planetary system," said Dennis Bodewits, professor of physics at Auburn University. "It tells us that the ingredients for life's chemistry are not unique to our own."[1]

items.title: Italy approves bill allowing naval blockades against migrant boats

featured_image.name: Italy's Meloni blames organised crime for 'alarming' migrant ...

items.description:
Italy's cabinet on Wednesday approved a bill authorizing naval blockades to halt migrant boats during periods of "exceptional pressure" at the nation's borders, a government source told Reuters. The legislation marks one of the most aggressive measures yet by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's right-wing government to curb irregular migration by sea.[1][2]

Under the draft law, the Italian government could prohibit vessels from entering territorial waters for up to six months in cases involving serious threats to public order or national security. Violators would face fines of up to €50,000, with repeat offenders risking confiscation of their vessels—a provision widely seen as targeting charity-operated rescue ships.[2][1]

items.title: Trump, Netanyahu end White House talks without deal on Iran

featured_image.name: Trump, Netanyahu end meeting with no deal on Iran - The Hill

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with President Donald Trump at the White House on Wednesday for roughly three hours, with Netanyahu expected to convey that the second phase of the Gaza ceasefire "is not moving," according to an Israeli source familiar with the discussions. The meeting, their sixth since Trump returned to office in January 2025, produced no definitive outcomes, Trump wrote on Truth Social afterward.[1][2][3][4]

"There was nothing definitive reached other than I insisted that negotiations with Iran continue to see whether or not a Deal can be consummated," Trump wrote, signaling a focus on U.S.-Iran diplomacy rather than the stalled Gaza framework.[5][1]

items.title: Trump weighs second carrier for Gulf as Iran talks resume

featured_image.name: Trump, Netanyahu to meet at White House in high-stakes talks on Iran, Gaza plan

items.description:
President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday that the United States would have to take "something very tough" against Iran if diplomatic efforts fail, as he considers deploying a second aircraft carrier to the Middle East and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu prepares to visit Washington.

In interviews with Axios and Fox Business Network, Trump said Tehran "very much wants to reach a deal" but cautioned that failure to reach an agreement would prompt severe consequences. "Either we make a deal, or we'll have to do something very tough — like last time," Trump told Axios, referencing last June's Operation Midnight Hammer, in which US forces struck three Iranian nuclear facilities at Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan.[1][2]

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $67,000 as 'Tinkerbell effect' fades

featured_image.name: Bitcoin bounce fades as it hovers around $67,000 - CNBC

items.description:
Bitcoin dropped below $67,000 on Wednesday, extending a sharp decline that has wiped roughly 40% from its October peak as investor confidence falters and the cryptocurrency's once-tight correlation with traditional equities weakens.

The world's largest cryptocurrency fell to approximately $66,996 early Wednesday morning before stabilizing near $67,000, according to market data. The decline marks a continuation of the sell-off that began when Bitcoin broke below the $70,000 threshold on February 5, triggering what analysts described as one of the most severe deleveraging events of the current cycle.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: MIT develops magnetic mixer to improve 3D bioprinting

featured_image.name: Magnetic mixer improves 3D bioprinting. MagMix, an onboard ...

items.description:
Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology have developed a magnetic mixing device called MagMix that addresses one of the most persistent challenges in 3D bioprinting: cells sinking to the bottom of printer syringes during long print sessions. The system, published February 2 in the journal Device, maintained uniform cell distribution across more than 45 minutes of continuous printing while preserving high cell viability.

The problem is simple gravity. Cells are heavier than the hydrogel "bio-inks" that carry them, causing them to settle during printing. "This cell settling, which becomes worse during the long print sessions required to print large tissues, leads to clogged nozzles, uneven cell distribution, and inconsistencies between printed tissues," explained Ritu Raman, the Eugene Bell Career Development Professor of Tissue Engineering and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at MIT.[1][2]

items.title: CME Group explores world's first rare earth futures contract

featured_image.name: CME hikes precious metal margins again after price swings ...

items.description:
CME Group is developing what would become the first futures contract for rare earth elements, according to three sources with knowledge of the matter who spoke to Reuters on Tuesday. The planned contract would combine neodymium and praseodymium—two critical materials used in electric vehicle motors, wind turbines, fighter jets, and drones—giving Western governments, companies, and financial institutions a new tool to hedge exposure to a market dominated by China.[1][2][3]

Rival Intercontinental Exchange is also exploring rare earth futures but is not as advanced in its planning as CME, two of the sources said. CME declined to comment, and ICE did not immediately respond to requests for comment.[2][1]
